title: Primitive Data Types
objectives: Describe int, double, float, decimal, char, bool, and string.
theory: A data type defines what a variable stores and which operations are valid. int stores signed whole numbers and commonly uses four bytes.
double uses eight bytes for general fractional calculations. float uses four bytes and requires an f suffix. Float is common in graphics and Unity APIs.
decimal uses sixteen bytes and high base-10 precision, making it suitable for money. Decimal literals use an m suffix.
char stores one character in single quotes. bool stores true or false. string stores text in double quotes.
Choose according to meaning, range, and precision. Float and double represent many decimal values approximately.
tryIt: Choose suitable types for age, average mark, balance, middle initial, enrolment status, and full name.
challenge: Build a product record using at least six different types and print every value.
mistakes: Use single quotes for char and double quotes for string.
Add f to float and m to decimal literals.
Do not store fractions in int.
summary: Types define valid values, memory, precision, and operations. Choose types according to the data's meaning.
quiz: Best type for number of lives?
A char uses single quotation marks.
